title: HR and Admin Assistant (Re-Advertised)
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a qualified HR and Admin Assistant for our operations in Dabat, Ethiopia.

Instruction for applicants:
All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered


Overall purpose of the role 

The HR and Admin Assistant is responsible for the efficient management of the HR, Admin and premises/warehouse functions at the field level. S/he ensures compliance with DRC’s policies and procedures and supports SS Team Leader in strengthening internal controls and accountability.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

Human Resources:


	Assist in ensuring staff compliance with human resources polices, as per DRC’s Operations Handbook and local HR Handbook.
	Ensure that leave, recruitment and training trackers are updated on a regular basis.
	Monitor staff attendance and ensure that all staff timesheets are submitted and filed on time.
	Assist in communicating with interview candidates and scheduling for tests and interviews.
	 Prepare employee contracts.
	Responsible for ensuring the following are accurate, complete and up to date: -personnel files, administration of health insurance scheme, social security,
	Assist managers and staff on effective performance management and administer the collation of performance management documentation
	Ensure new staff receive an appropriate orientation and induction. Support staff development activities including promoting the DRC Learning Catalogue.
	Ensure clearance and debriefing is carried out for exiting staff.


 Administration:


	Ensure that all office systems and equipment (power, water, telephone, photocopier, fax, etc.) are in good working order.
	Payment of office and guest house bills.
	Responsible for office supplies.
	Responsible for necessary repairs & maintenance in a timely manner in coordination with the Logistics staff.
	Manage all contract arrangements with lessors and ensuring that contractual obligations are adhered to.
	 Establish central mail recording system and filing system.
	Ensure that DRC staff have Identification cards (ID) with the period of validity in accordance with the employment contract.


Warehouse/Premises Support:


	Work closely with the Supply Chain team to support stock receipt, recordkeeping, and proper storage where necessary.
	Support the Area Manager in conducting periodic checks of premises and supplies (e.g., fire extinguishers, fuel stock).
	Ensure inventory forms and casual contracts (cleaners, cooks, etc.) are documented and archived


Procurement:


	To manage all procurement activities at the emergency office (P2P) goods, service, work within the approved threshold.
	Implement the procurement plans.


Experience and technical competencies: 


	Minimum 1 year's relevant work experience in similar field.
	Familiarity with ERP systems (e.g., DYN) and high proficiency in Microsoft Office (especially Excel).
	Solid understanding of Ethiopian labor law and administrative procedures.
	Experience with HR practices, staff coordination, and logistics is desirable.
	Strong organizational and interpersonal skills; ability to multitask under pressure.


EDUCATION: (include certificates, licenses, etc.)


	Diploma in HR Management, Business Administration or equivalent professional qualification


LANGUAGE: (indicate Fluency level)


	Advanced spoken and written English 
	Proficiency in (Amharic) preferred. 


 

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies: 

Striving for excellence: You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process. 

Collaborating: You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback. 

Taking the lead: You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation. 

Communicating: You listen and speak effectively and honestly. 

Demonstrating integrity: You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

We offer

Contract length: 12 Months

Contract Type: National Contract

Band: I2 – Non-Management

Designation of Duty Station: Dabat, Ethiopia

Start date:  15th October 2026

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for National employees

Application process

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than three pages) in English. Applications sent by email will not be considered

Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered.

Closing date for applications: September 28, 2026

For further information about the Danish Refugee Council, please consult our website drc.ngo.

title: Protection Officer - Return, Reintegration & Mixed Migration
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified Protection Officer

About the job

The Protection Officer is responsible for field-level coordination, implementation and quality assurance of DRC's SIDA P2P protection, return/reintegration and related Economic Recovery linkages in Bosaso and relevant Eastern Route return and transit locations in Puntland. The role supports timely, protection-sensitive delivery of DRC direct activities and field-level accompaniment of local partners across vulnerability screening/case management, PSS, IPA and referrals, route-based Protection Monitoring, reintegration follow-up, livelihoods linkages and systems strengthening.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

Protection services, case management and direct assistance


	Coordinate vulnerability screening and protection risk assessment for migrants and returnees and support safe, rights-based case management and referral follow-up in line with DRC SOPs, informed consent, confidentiality and Do No Harm.
	Provide field-level technical guidance to assigned DRC caseworkers and support quality of partner case-management/referral delivery as delegated; ensure GBV, Child Protection, trafficking and other specialized concerns are safely identified and referred.
	Coordinate approved IPA and other immediate protection support, and facilitate safe referrals to MHPSS, health, legal aid, shelter/housing, civil documentation, livelihoods and other specialized services based on assessed needs.


 PSS, return/reintegration and Economic Recovery linkages


	Coordinate/support delivery of structured individual and group PSS and appropriate referral to specialized MHPSS services.
	Support dignified reception, protection screening, information and counselling, access to hotline services, documentation, individualized reintegration planning and structured post-return follow-up, including through the Bosaso MRC and other P2P service points as relevant.
	Work closely with Economic Recovery colleagues and partners to link returnees to market-informed skills, employment/self-employment, business/start-up and financial-inclusion pathways, ensuring protection barriers and safeguarding considerations are integrated.


 Protection Monitoring, referral systems and evidence


	Coordinate regular community and route-based Protection Monitoring in assigned locations; provide day-to-day technical guidance to Protection Monitors/enumerators and ensure urgent protection risks and referral needs trigger appropriate response.
	Support service mapping and referral/RMS strengthening, monitor referral functionality, and contribute to the Ethiopia-Somalia cross-border case-management/legal-aid pilot in line with agreed consent, confidentiality and data-protection protocols.
	Use anonymized Protection Monitoring and referral trends to inform programme adaptation, reporting, validation and evidence/advocacy, keeping confidential case data separate from routine monitoring/MEAL datasets.


 Partner, government and stakeholder coordination


	Provide field-level technical accompaniment to KAALO, participate in joint monitoring with government counterparts and KAALO, and follow up agreed capacity-strengthening actions on Protection, referrals, PSS, Protection Monitoring and rights-based return/reintegration.
	Support existing government-led migration, referral and reintegration systems through joint monitoring, dialogue, practical coordination and on-the-job support, strengthening rather than creating parallel mechanisms.
	Coordinate with authorities, MRCs, service providers, community structures and humanitarian/protection actors, and support relevant reintegration, social-cohesion and stakeholder-engagement activities as assigned.


 Planning, monitoring, reporting and compliance


	Maintain field activity plans and monitor delivery against approved workplans, budgets, targets and programme-quality standards; identify implementation gaps and support timely corrective action.
	Coordinate with MEAL/IM, Economic Recovery, Partnerships/Grants, Finance and relevant programme/area teams; maintain accurate programme documentation and timely activity/technical reporting.
	Ensure implementation complies with DRC policies and donor requirements, safeguarding/PSEA/AAP commitments, core Protection principles, confidentiality and responsible data management.


About you

To be successful in this role we expect you to have:

Required 


	Minimum 3 years of relevant Protection experience in humanitarian, displacement or mixed-migration settings; experience in return/reintegration is strongly preferred.
	Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Psychology, Sociology, Human Rights, International Development, Peace and Conflict Studies, or a closely related field.
	Demonstrated experience in case management/referrals, PSS, Protection Monitoring and protection-sensitive direct assistance.
	Relevant training in Protect

title: Technical Specialist ( Protection)
description:
Job Technical Specialist (Protection)

The Danish Refugee Council (DRC), one of the world’s leading NGOs, with a focus on responding to displacement, have been registered in Sudan since 2004, delivering life-saving programming in protection, emergency response, shelter, food security and livelihoods, disaster risk reduction, camp management, and humanitarian mine action. DRC has implemented projects in Central Darfur, South Kordofan, Gedaref, Port Sudan, and White Nile. Sudan hosts one of the largest displaced populations in Africa, with over 3.7 million internally displaced people and over 1.1 million refugees from South Sudan, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Central African Republic, Chad, Yemen and Syria. Against a background of political crisis, Sudan faces economic and social turmoil, with sharp increases in food and energy costs, further exacerbated by disease outbreaks and ongoing conflict.

POSITION PROFILE

Overall purpose of the role:

 Under the supervision of the Chief of Party, the Technical Specialist contributes to the development and implementation and the technical coordination of the FCDO funded consortia programme in Sudan. He/She is responsible for coordinating high-quality technical services, in close collaboration with consortium partners. To this aim, the Technical Specialist will support the enhancement of risk mitigation, response and prevention activities especially contextualization of social norm methodologies, harmonization and rollout of tools, guidelines and SOPs for case management, coordinate continuous capacity building and ensure standard donor and data analysis/reporting methods (in collaboration with PIM Specialist and MEAL) are in place for these activities. Additionally, the Technical Specialist will support harmonising Safeguarding mechanisms and processes 

.DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Main Responsibilities:


	Responsible for providing coordination and direction to the Consortium on technical activities
	Ensure the consortium has a coherent technical strategy that responds to the requirements of people the project intends to support, with necessary safeguarding measures in place
	Provide regular technical support and guidance to Consortium Technical focal points to strengthen the capacity of protection teams in delivering high quality GBV mitigation, prevention and response 
	In collaboration with the Consortium Technical focal points and in alignment with Sudan GBV AoR guidance, coordinate, harmonise and roll out  GBV case management SOP (including Cash for Protection, individual PSS and referral mechanism) as well as guidance on RESCUE pot and other related tools
	In collaboration with the Consortium technical focal points enhance GBV prevention efforts especially through supporting the coordination of contextualizing and overseeing social norm methodologies 
	Support partners in the set up and development of WGSS SoPs, use of PSS curricula, gender-sensitive awareness raising messaging and community engagement 
	Ensure a minimum standard of capacity and awareness on GBV referrals across protection teams (including sensitive legal cases) and other sector teams to reinforce the effectiveness of the more specialized staff response
	Ensure Do no Harm through coordinating and harmonising effective coaching, mentorship, and trainings required for implementation - ensuring ToR and monitoring is in place for various capacity development initativies across the delivery chain
	Undertake field visits to monitor the quality of implementation and provide technical advice and customized and needs based capacity building to protection staff
	In collaboration with PIM Specialist Ensure that ethnical, consistent and sound data collection management systems are in place for GBV protection activities, ensuing availability of data analysis for informed decision making and project design; 
	Support consortium technical focal points with the adoption of standardized methodologies (including those developed by consultants or internally) related to GBV, including associated monitoring and evaluation mechanisms; 
	Responsible for reviewing and collating the technical activities for donor and other external reports (as required)
	Stay abreast of developments that have an impact on the protection environment in Sudan and provide ongoing analysis on key issues on a regular basis.
	Identify challenges, bottlenecks and quality concerns and risks of doing harm related to GBV programming and escalate when needed, while taking lead on identifying possible solutions
	Serve as PSEAH/Safeguarding focal point for the consortium management unit 


Capacity building 


	Lead the coordination, and when requested, development and delivery of participatory training materials, for downstream consortium members with ongoing coaching, mentorship, and training required for implementation of GBV programming

title: Information Management Specialist
description:
Job Title Information Management (IM) Specialist

The Danish Refugee Council (DRC), one of the world’s leading NGOs, with a focus on responding to displacement, have been registered in Sudan since 2004, delivering life-saving programming in protection, emergency response, shelter, food security and livelihoods, disaster risk reduction, camp management, and humanitarian mine action. DRC has implemented projects in Central Darfur, South Kordofan, Gedaref, Port Sudan, and White Nile. Sudan hosts one of the largest displaced populations in Africa, with over 3.7 million internally displaced people and over 1.1 million refugees from South Sudan, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Central African Republic, Chad, Yemen and Syria. Against a background of political crisis, Sudan faces economic and social turmoil, with sharp increases in food and energy costs, further exacerbated by disease outbreaks and ongoing conflict.

POSITION PROFILE

Overall purpose of the role:

The Information Management (IM) Specialist will be responsible for the set up and roll-out of a coordinated and consolidated information management system for the FCDO HOPE S programme.  This includes development of a common database tool, development of a PowerBI dashboard, maintaining IM information, data cleaning, and carrying out data analysis process for monitoring data collected across the consortium.

The position will support the MEAL Coordinator in ensuring quality quantitative and qualitative data analysis, and will be responsible for the design, implementation, and management of program-related data collection and information management systems. The position will play a key role in contributing and supporting programming and advocacy through streamlining the collection, analysis, and sharing of information in accordance with professional standards. This work will further contribute to improved, evidence-based programming through improving the production and analysis quality of IM products, including monitoring reports and rapid assessment snapshots to be shared internally and externally to key stakeholders.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Responsibilities

Information Management 

Ensure the set-up of a harmonized interoperable information management system that facilitates data sharing and coordination across the consortium and feeds into the wider protection analysis in Sudan


	Overall responsible for the development of Consortium’s information management systems seeking feedback from consortium on PIM matrix system, tools, and approaches and using systematized and collaborative framework. 
	Maintain and regularly update Consortium’s information systems, including databases and dashboards, to ensure data accuracy, accessibility, and security.
	Lead on developing, rolling out and regularly updating PowerBI dashboard based on newly developed data collection toolset (as agreed with technical focal points on the regularity)
	Responsible for collecting, assessing, analyzing, and disseminating information (quality reports, dashboard information, etc) with the relevant key stakeholders 
	Produce programme snapshots and dashboards on a monthly basis, highlighting key issues and trends in coordination with Consortium while maintaining GBVIM minimum standards, GDPR minimum standards, donor and DRC data protection policies. 
	Support the production of thematic reports or other IM materials in consultation with Consortium partners
	Process data, compile and disseminate information for use in various protection-related materials, including but not limited to reports, briefings and analysis
	Provide IM technical support to consortium IM focal points, including ongoing training and capacity building Lead on Information Management, including data collection processes and protocols, and monitoring tools.
	Work collaboratively with RIMS team, acting as a focal point for the consortium in the set up/roll out of training on using referral information management system
	Support on service mapping and documenting guidance on referral pathways
	Undertake other tasks as requested by the Chief of Party


Data Quality and Protection:


	Ensure data protection and confidentiality are maintained in line with DRC’s data protection policies, FCDO policies & GBV IMS/GDPR minimum standards, ensuring Data Sharing Agreements are in place and key components of the DSA are understood and rolled out/implemented
	Responsible for storing and maintaining data for the consortium as per GDPR guidance/GBV IM Standards
	Develop and implement data quality assurance processes to ensure the accuracy, reliability, and timeliness of data collected across programs.
	Regularly review and audit data collection processes to identify and address potential issues in data quality and security.
	Conduct quality checks on collected data to ensure quality of data collection and reporting. 
	Support CMU to maintain its knowledge base by acting as the focal point for consortium share point folder.

title: Engagement Coordinator
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a qualified Engagement Coordinator for our operations in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

Instruction for applicants:
All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered


Overall purpose of the role 

INGO Group Secretariat consists of dedicated staff members responsible for facilitating information sharing, coordination, representation, advocacy, and support to member organizations. The Secretariat is overseen by a Steering Committee composed of Country Directors and is a project of the Danish Refugee Council (DRC).

While the INGO Group engages extensively at the national level, members have consistently identified the need for stronger information sharing, representation, and operational support to coordination at the sub-national level. Humanitarian actors operating across Ethiopia face increasingly complex realities that require systematic engagement with authorities, humanitarian partners, and other stakeholders.

The engagement Coordinator is a senior coordination position responsible for supporting humanitarian and resilience operations through enhanced coordination, information exchange, and collective engagement among INGO Group members at the regional level. The position supports humanitarian actors operating in regions where significant responses are being implemented and serves as the primary link between regional coordination structures and the national-level INGO Group.

The role focuses on identifying and addressing operational challenges affecting the response, facilitating collective analysis and problem-solving, supporting access, promoting information sharing, and ensuring that regional operational realities inform national-level representation, advocacy and engagement efforts.

The postholder will facilitate, support and participate in the work of regional INGO platforms, the Humanitarian Leads Working Group, and other operational working groups as required. The role will engage actively with regional government authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, donors and other relevant stakeholders to promote an enabling environment for principled and effective humanitarian action.

The position reports directly to the INGO Group Manager and may provide regular briefings and recommendations to the Steering Committee as required.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

Sub National Coordination, representation and stakeholder engagement 


	Strengthen and support regional INGO coordination platforms in areas where significant numbers of members operate.
	Facilitate coordination, collaboration and information sharing among humanitarian directors, area managers, operational focal points and member organizations.
	Serve as the principal link between regional coordination structures and the national INGO Group Secretariat, ensuring that regional operational realities inform national-level engagement.
	Establish and maintain productive relationships with regional authorities, UN agencies, donors, NGOs and other relevant stakeholders.
	Represent the INGO Group in relevant sub-national coordination forums and external engagements in accordance with agreed positions and messaging.
	Support collective engagement on operational challenges, humanitarian priorities and emerging response needs.
	Promote collaboration and cooperation among humanitarian actors to strengthen the quality and effectiveness of humanitarian operations especially through the Area based coordination structures.


 Operational support and working group facilitation


	Monitor, analyze and support collective action on operational constraints affecting humanitarian actors, including access, bureaucratic and administrative challenges.
	Facilitate the Humanitarian Leads Working Group and other operational or thematic working groups established by the INGO Group.
	Support working group leads and platform focal points in defining priorities, facilitating discussions and following up on agreed actions.
	Promote information sharing, collective analysis and problem-solving among members operating at sub-national level.
	Identify opportunities for coordinated approaches to common operational challenges and facilitate collective engagement where appropriate.
	Support the development of operational guidance, recommendations, briefing materials and coordination tools for Area Based Coordination structures.
	Promote cross-learning, exchange of good practices and operational collaboration among members across different regions


Analysis, information management and member support 


	Monitor political, humanitarian, policy and security developments affecting operations in Ethiopia.
	Produce and disseminate analytical products, updates, briefing notes and summaries for members and the Secretariat.

title: Economic Recovery Specialist - Financial Inclusion & Market System Development
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified Economic Recovery Specialist – Financial Inclusion & Market System Development for our operations in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

Instruction for applicants:
All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered


Overall purpose of the role 

The Economic Recovery Specialist is the techninical lead of the implementation of the economic recovery component of the Mixed Migration The Economic Recovery Specialist is the senior technical lead for local economic pathways under the Mixed Migration Programme. The Specialist is responsible for designing, strengthening and quality assuring market oriented, protection sensitive and climate resilient economic pathways that enable migrants, returnees, transit populations, at risk youth and other vulnerable people on the move to access decent employment, apprenticeships, enterprise opportunities, financial services and sustainable livelihoods.

The Specialist applies a Market Systems Development approach to understand and address the constraints that prevent people on the move from accessing and sustaining economic opportunities. Rather than relying on uniform livelihood packages, the Specialist ensures that programme support responds to participant skills, experience, aspirations, documentation status, mobility intentions, household circumstances and actual labour market demand.

The Specialist leads the technical development of the economic pathway model, strengthens relationships with employers and other market actors, and ensures that DRC support contributes to functioning and sustainable market systems rather than creating parallel or permanently subsidised services.

The Specialist works closely with the Protection, MEAL, Programme Management and Economic Recovery Officers to ensure that local economic pathways and regular labour mobility pathways are connected where appropriate.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

1. Economic Pathways, Counselling and Referral


	Lead the design and continuous refinement of socioeconomic and skills profiling tools and the individualised economic pathway methodology used at Migration Resource Centres, transit hubs, GreenHubs and relevant return locations.
	Establish technical standards and quality assurance mechanisms for economic counselling and pathway selection, ensuring that pathways are based on participant capacities, aspirations, documentation status, protection considerations, mobility intentions and actual market opportunities.
	Lead the development of differentiated economic pathways covering employment, apprenticeships, enterprise development, self employment, financial services, skills development and other appropriate economic opportunities.
	Develop and maintain a dynamic, route based mapping of livelihood, employment, apprenticeship, training, enterprise, financial inclusion and reintegration services and opportunities.
	Lead the strengthening of internal and external referral mechanisms so participants can access appropriate services beyond direct DRC assistance.
	Ensure that economic pathway decisions are protection sensitive and that participants are not referred toward unsafe employment, exploitative conditions, fraudulent recruitment or other known protection risks.
	Provide technical leadership for GreenHub economic pathway assessment, incubation, coaching, mentorship and seed capital models where relevant.
	Establish criteria and quality standards for determining when direct economic support, referral, market linkage or other forms of assistance are most appropriate.
	Ensure that entrepreneurship support is differentiated according to participant capacity, business experience, market opportunity and access to finance rather than delivered as a standard package.
	Lead the development of financial literacy and access to finance approaches appropriate to participants' economic circumstances, mobility profiles and documentation status.
	Build and manage strategic partnerships with banks, MFIs, digital financial service providers and other appropriate financial actors.
	Identify barriers preventing participants from accessing formal and digital financial services and work with relevant actors to identify feasible solutions.
	Engage financial service providers and enterprise support actors in adapting products, services or delivery models where feasible and consistent with programme objectives.
	Build partnerships with BDS providers, TVETs, business associations and other enterprise support actors to expand access to sustainable services.

Overall purpose of the role 

The Economic Recovery Specialist is the technical lead for the implementation of the economic recovery component of the Mixed Migration Programme, with a particular focus on employment pathways, market oriented apprenticeships, employer engagement, skills to employment linkages and labour market integration.

The Specialist is responsible for designing, strengthening and quality assuring market oriented and protection sensitive economic pathways that enable migrants, returnees, transit populations, at risk youth and other vulnerable people on the move to access decent employment, paid apprenticeships, skills recognition and certification, and other viable income generating opportunities.

The Specialist applies a Market Systems Development approach to identify and address the constraints that prevent people on the move from accessing and sustaining employment opportunities. Rather than relying on standardised livelihood packages, the Specialist ensures that programme support responds to participant skills, experience, aspirations, documentation status, mobility intentions and actual employer and labour market demand.

The Specialist leads the technical development of employment and apprenticeship pathways, strengthens relationships with employers and other labour market actors, and ensures that programme interventions contribute to improved labour absorption and sustainable employment rather than creating parallel or permanently subsidised employment mechanisms.

The Specialist works closely with Economic Recovery Officers, the Labour Mobility & Skills Recognition Officer, Protection, MEAL and Programme Management to ensure that participants are appropriately profiled, referred and supported across skills recognition, apprenticeships, employment and regular labour mobility pathways

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

1. Labour Market Engagement, Employment Pathways & Private Sector Partnerships


	Lead analysis of high demand sectors, occupations, skills gaps, employer recruitment practices and barriers affecting migrants, returnees and at risk youth.
	Design market oriented employment pathways that respond to real labour demand and participant profiles.
	Build and manage strategic relationships with employers, industry associations, business networks and other labour market actors.
	Identify systemic barriers to recruitment, retention and advancement and develop practical responses with market actors.
	Facilitate linkages between participants and employers through authorised employment services and referral mechanisms.
	Strengthen approaches that enable employers and market actors to contribute placements, supervision, technical expertise, resources or other forms of support.
	Oversee placement, retention and transition tracking and use findings for continuous improvement.


2. Market Oriented Paid Apprenticeships & Employer Incentives


	Lead the design, quality assurance and adaptive management of paid apprenticeship models in high demand sectors with realistic pathways into employment or self employment.
	Establish clear criteria for employer selection and ensure apprenticeships promote decent work, occupational safety, non discrimination and protection.
	Provide technical guidance on apprenticeship duration, workplace learning, supervision and transition planning.
	Design and oversee time bound, market aligned employer support or incentive mechanisms that increase labour absorption without creating long term subsidy dependence.
	Work with employers to address practical constraints related to recruitment, onboarding, supervision and retention, while encouraging them to contribute their own resources and expertise.
	Document lessons and continuously refine apprenticeship and incentive models based on employer and participant evidence.
	3. Skills Recognition, Participant Placement & Employability
	Strengthen pathways linking prior informal skills to competency assessment, certification and employment, in close coordination with the Labour Mobility & Skills Recognition Officer, MoLS, CoC centres and TVETs.
	Prioritise occupations for skills recognition based on employer demand and labour market evidence, ensuring certification is linked to concrete employment opportunities.
	Establish practical systems for matching and placing participants into apprenticeships, employment and other economic opportunities.
